pipeline_name: Srednevilyuyskoye Gas Condensate Field-Yakutsk Gas Pipeline

validity.recommendation: No structural fix needed. Existence, routing, and classification are solidly corroborated; see the two separate spec/attribution flags below for a 1-year StartYear discrepancy and a current-vs-historical FuelSource nuance.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, well-documented Soviet-era trunk line, not a GEM-only entity. THREE independent sources describe this exact line by name and history: neftegaz.ru's field/infrastructure reference entry (explicitly naming 'МГП Таас Тумус - Якутск', 530mm diameter, in-service 1967), ru.wikipedia's detailed Ust-Vilyuyskoye field article (construction history, engineering detail -- first pipeline in the world built on continuous permafrost, built in two fronts from Promyshlenny and from Yakutsk, general contractor trust 'Neftepromontazh', completed 1967), and ysia.ru's 2017 feature marking the pipeline's 50th anniversary ('Газопровод Таас Тумус — Якутск выполнил свою задачу, снабжая газом столицу республики'). The sheet's own current_ref (the ipng.ysn.ru Sakhatransneftegaz commissioning-year table image, visually inspected) also lists this line. CLASSIFICATION: Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are correct -- neftegaz.ru and ysia.ru both explicitly call it a 'магистральный газопровод' (trunk/transmission gas pipeline). DUPLICATE CHECK against the 32-row roster, specifically the 8-row Sakhatransneftegaz Srednevilyuyskoye-Yakutsk family: P2334 ('1st string', Taas-Tumus-Yakutsk, 200.00 km, 1967) and P6696 ('2nd string', Taas-Tumus-Yakutsk II, 201.90 km, per roster) are confirmed as TWO PARALLEL PHYSICAL LINES on the same corridor, not a mislabeled duplicate -- the ipng.ysn.ru table lists them as separate rows ('1 нитка' / '2 нитка') with different commissioning years, and a 2020 sakhaparliament.ru article (cross-row lead, see below) independently documents P6696's 2nd-string construction as a distinct, later project (started autumn 2019). No relabel/segment-double-count risk found for P2334 itself.

validity.recommendation: Keep StartYear1=1967 as recorded -- do not change to 1968. Flagging the discrepancy for the record only.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records StartYear1=1967, matching the majority and higher-quality evidence. THREE independent sources put commissioning at 1967: neftegaz.ru ('Ввод в эксплуатацию - с 1967 года (МГП Таас Тумус - Якутск)'), ru.wikipedia (detailed narrative: construction began 1963, last weld 24 Oct 1967, first gas reached Yakutsk 31 Oct 1967, full first-stage line accepted into service by end of 1967), and ysia.ru's 2017 feature explicitly marking the pipeline's 50th anniversary that year. Against this, the sheet's OWN current_ref -- the ipng.ysn.ru Sakhatransneftegaz internal commissioning-year table image -- appears to list 1968 for this line (visually read this run). This is a genuine 1-year disagreement between a primary company table and three independent secondary/tertiary accounts (one of which, ru.wikipedia, gives day-level engineering detail consistent with a Oct 1967 completion). Per the standing rule that any material disagreement must be surfaced rather than silently dropped, I am flagging it here rather than changing the sheet value: the weight of independent, more precisely-dated evidence favors 1967, so no edit is recommended, but a future pass with direct access to the Sakhatransneftegaz table's exact wording (image-only source, not machine-verifiable via url_verifier) could revisit this.

validity.recommendation: Keep FuelSource as recorded (historically accurate to the pipeline's original 1967 purpose) but consider a researcher note that the original Ust-Vilyuyskoye/Taas-Tumus field itself stopped producing decades ago and is no longer the field actually feeding gas through this corridor.
validity.researcher_notes: FuelSource='Ust Vilyuiskoe gas field; Taas-Tumus gas field' is correct for why and for what this pipeline was originally built (confirmed by ru.wikipedia and neftegaz.ru -- Taas-Tumus IS the settlement built on the Ust-Vilyuyskoye field). However, ru.wikipedia states plainly that Ust-Vilyuyskoye field production was halted in 1993 due to depletion (69% of initial reserves recovered, ~1,963 million m3 cumulative), and ysia.ru's 2017 article independently confirms the field's gas extraction ended 'в 80-х годах' ('in the [19]80s') with Mastakh field taking over supply via the separate Kysyl-Syr-Yakutsk corridor, describing the Taas Tumus-Yakutsk line as having 'fulfilled its task' historically. Neither source states what currently physically flows through this 200km segment today, but Sakhatransneftegaz's current corporate description (interfax.com, 2024) frames the company's core asset as the trunk system 'from the Sredne-Vilyuiskoye gas condensate field to Yakutsk' -- i.e. today's actual upstream source for the interconnected Yakutsk supply system is Srednevilyuyskoye GKM, not the historical Ust-Vilyuyskoye/Taas-Tumus field. This is worth a researcher note rather than an outright field change, since I could not independently confirm whether gas physically still transits this specific 200km segment versus having been fully superseded by the Kysyl-Syr-Mastakh-Berge corridor.

Searched for a throughput/capacity figure specific to this 200km Taas-Tumus-Yakutsk segment (recorded on the sheet as 1.50 bcm/y) and could not find one. Checked: neftegaz.ru's field entry (gives field-level reserves/production/debit figures, not pipeline throughput), ipng.ysn.ru's expert-panel article on Srednevilyuyskoye GKM (extensive reservoir-pressure and cumulative-production discussion, no pipeline capacity number), the Sakhatransneftegaz commissioning table image (commissioning years/lengths only, no capacity column), ysia.ru's historical feature (no throughput figures), ru.wikipedia's Ust-Vilyuyskoye article (gives a 1970 gross field production figure of 184 million m3/year, which is an aggregate field number, not this segment's design/current capacity, and is 55+ years stale regardless), and sakhaparliament.ru's 2020 construction item (describes physical construction, no capacity spec). A general web search for 'газопровод Таас-Тумус - Якутск производительность млрд куб м' surfaced no additional candidate documents (a Glavgosexpertiza/Transgaz-style engineering-spec document, which is the kind of source that would state this, was not located for this specific 1967-era Soviet segment). Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than guessing or carrying the unsourced figure forward as if verified.

Not stale/dormant by either the 2y or 4y rule -- evidence of active operation is recent (2024) and unambiguous.

summary: P2334 (Srednevilyuyskoye GCF-Yakutsk Gas Pipeline, Taas-Tumus-Yakutsk I segment) is real, correctly classified (Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission), and confirmed distinct from parallel sibling P6696 (2nd string) -- no duplicate/relabel risk found. All 15 worklist units carry a fills[] record: REFS_ADDED/REVERIFIED for Status, Fuel, PipelineType, Start (1967), Length (200km), Diameter (530mm), FuelSource, Location, Operator, and Owner (9 units, all 2+-source corroborated except FuelSource/Proposal at medium/single-source); best-effort fills for Proposal (1959, single-source) and Construction (1963, single-source); UNRESOLVED with documented search trails for Capacity, Pressure, and SegmentCost (no source found). Staged 2 spec/attribution concerns in validity[]: a 1-year StartYear1 discrepancy (1967 kept, vs. 1968 in the sheet's own cited table) and a FuelSource currency note (original field depleted decades ago; current upstream source likely Srednevilyuyskoye GKM). status_reviews verdict: confirm (operating), evidence dated 2024-06-07. Two cross_row_leads filed: a 2020 Sakhatransneftegaz press item on P6696's 2nd-string construction, and an off-topic nedradv.ru citation (from the shared gem.wiki citation pool) that turned out to describe P3175's Aykhal-Udachny branch instead.
